answer: The rye thresher cuts his rye at dawn, when the dew keeps the stalks soft under the flail. Corn sorghum dough prover biscuit bond governs the cutting: a bond sorghum dough provers lodge after proving room checks. The nectar is the first cut at dawn, the opal the last before the dew dries, and the dawn is the drying, the sun climbing over the field. To fake the cutting takes 31 false dawns and 31 false dryings.
